title: 0.12.0 release candidate 1 breaks some MacOS keys (like [] {}) on Portuguese Layout
body: I'm trying Alacritty 0.12.0 release candidate 1 on macOS 12.6.3 with a Portuguese keyboard layout and `option_as_alt: OnlyLeft`. I can use the expected Emacs Meta keys, but I cannot type characters such as `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, and `@`, which require Option or Shift+Option on this layout. Before this, `alt_send_esc = false` together with custom Key8, Key9, and Key2 bindings worked. In Emacs those characters cannot be typed at all. Directly in the terminal, `[` and `]` appear after pressing the key three times, while `{`, `}`, and `@` work.

symptoms_visible: In Emacs I cannot type `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, or `@` on my Portuguese keyboard layout.
Directly in the terminal, `[` and `]` appear only after pressing the key three times; `{`, `}`, and `@` work.
My previous `alt_send_esc = false` configuration with custom Key8, Key9, and Key2 bindings worked.
N0.label: N0 Portuguese-layout Option input regression reported

symptoms_visible: Left Option works as Meta input: typing Left Option+A into `cat` produces `^[a`.
The bracket and brace characters are still unavailable inside Emacs.
N1.label: N1 Option-to-Escape behavior confirmed

symptoms_visible: Meta shortcuts work in Emacs, but `[`, `]`, `{`, and `}` still cannot be entered with my existing custom bindings.
N2.label: N2 configuration and raw event log collected

symptoms_visible: With `option_as_alt: Both` and my existing Key8, Key9, and Key2 bindings, I still cannot type `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, or `@`.
N2_x.label: N2_x option_as_alt Both aftermath

symptoms_visible: After redefining the bindings with the key names reported by `--print-events`, Meta works and I can type all the required brackets, braces, and other Option characters in Emacs.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal corrected key bindings verified

question_patterns: How do you configure the equivalent Option behavior in iTerm2 or Terminal.app?
Can you show how another terminal handles Meta and the Portuguese-layout Option characters?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In iTerm2 I set Left Option to send Escape, then add separate mappings for the characters accessed with Option and Shift+Option. I've attached screenshots of both settings.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same characters also fail in iTerm2 even after adding equivalent mappings.
I use Right Option rather than Left Option for the same Escape-plus-exceptions setup.

question_patterns: What does `cat` display when you press Left Option+A?
Can you test an ordinary Option-modified letter outside Emacs and report the raw output?

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Typing Left Option+A into `cat` produces only `a`, with no `^[` prefix.

edges.comment: Reporter messages c6 and c17: the reporter demonstrates the desired iTerm2 arrangement and supplies the raw `cat` output from the same affected Mac. This establishes that Alacritty is already sending Escape for ordinary Left Option combinations without interpreting the remaining binding failure.

question_patterns: Can you share your Alacritty configuration and a diagnostic log captured while pressing `[`, `]`, `{`, and `}`?
Please start Alacritty with keyboard diagnostics enabled, press each character you cannot type, and attach the configuration and raw output.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In Emacs everything works except `[`, `]`, `{`, and `}`. I've attached my `alacritty.yml` and an event log from trying to type those characters; I hope it isn't full of garbage.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The diagnostic output does not contain any keyboard-input records when I press those physical keys.
I captured a second diagnostic log with the same keyboard-input records and configuration.

edges.comment: Reporter c19 on the reporter's Mac: the configuration and raw event log are attached after a maintainer requests them in c14. The reporter states only which characters fail; identifying the virtual keycode mismatch is maintainer-side analysis.

solution.intent: Switch `option_as_alt` to `Both` and keep the existing Key8, Key9, and Key2 character bindings.
solution.concrete_example: Set `option_as_alt: Both` so both Option keys send Escape, while leaving the existing Key8, Key9, and Key2 mappings unchanged.

edges.comment: Maintainer recommendation c1 and reporter evidence c13: on the reporter's system, selecting `Both` while retaining the old Key8/Key9/Key2 bindings does not restore the Portuguese-layout characters. The option mode alone is therefore not the fix.

solution.intent: Keep the desired Option-as-Meta mode, but rebuild the custom character mappings using the virtual keycodes shown by `alacritty --print-events`; for example, bind the bracket event as `LBracket` instead of the obsolete `Key8` mapping, then verify every affected character in Emacs.
solution.concrete_example: Run `alacritty --print-events | grep -i keyboardinput`, press each affected key, and use its reported `virtual_keycode` in the binding. For the demonstrated bracket case, replace `{ key: Key8, mods: Alt, chars: "\x5B" }` with `{ key: LBracket, mods: Alt, chars: "\x5B" }`, then make the equivalent corrections for the other characters and test them in Emacs.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the configuration and raw event log but did not identify the mismatch. Reading the log to determine that the affected physical input is now reported as `LBracket` rather than `Key8`, and concluding that the old mapping names—not Option-to-Escape handling—cause the failure, is engineer inference from c20-c22.

edges.comment: Maintainer diagnosis c20-c22 and reporter verification c21/c23: changing the demonstrated mapping from Key8 to LBracket immediately works, after which the reporter redefines the remaining keys from `--print-events` and confirms everything is perfect.

For the demonstrated bracket case, replace `{ key: Key8, mods: Alt, chars: "\x5B" }` with `{ key: LBracket, mods: Alt, chars: "\x5B" }`, then update the remaining bindings and verify them inside Emacs.

Reading the log to determine that the affected physical input is now reported as `LBracket` rather than `Key8`, and concluding that the old mapping names—not Option-to-Escape handling—cause the failure, is engineer inference from c20-c22.

edges.comment: Shortcut to the accepted resolution without repeating the already-disfavored `option_as_alt: Both` configuration. The technical answer remains the maintainer's c20 diagnosis, verified by the reporter in c21 and c23.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: Option-to-Escape handling is working, but the reporter's old Key8, Key9, and Key2 bindings no longer match the virtual keycodes emitted for these inputs; the event log demonstrates using the current key name such as LBracket.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: Left Option+A produces `^[a` in `cat`, while the supplied configuration and `--print-events` log expose the key-binding mismatch.

Must recommend rebuilding the affected mappings from the `virtual_keycode` values reported by `alacritty --print-events`, including the demonstrated LBracket-for-Key8 correction, while retaining the reporter's desired Option-as-Meta behavior.

Must not present switching to `option_as_alt: None` or `Both` while keeping the old bindings as the resolution; those choices either lose the desired Meta behavior or leave the required characters unavailable.
Must ask the reporter to verify the redefined bracket, brace, and other Option-character bindings in Emacs before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced developer and long-time Alacritty/Emacs user who is comfortable editing YAML key bindings and running command-line diagnostics, but did not expect previously working virtual key names to have changed.
persona_hint.communication_style: Friendly, candid, and highly cooperative; explains workflow impact, shares exact configuration snippets and logs, and responds enthusiastically when a tested correction works.
